text:
Nikolaj Ehlers already has a Cup in Carolina, and he's playing like the Hurricanes' transition engine. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season, carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries, with 52% of his shots coming off the rush. That's a winger who turns a turnover into a chance before the defense can set.

This season reads the same. Carolina owns 60% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, and his ten points in his last ten games beat what our numbers expected (7.8). He's doing it in 16:13 a night, so this is efficient work.

The goals lag: four on 5.24 expected, shooting 9.5% against a range centered near 12.6%. That should come up. Evolving-Hockey had him 16th among 401 forwards last season at 2.9 wins above replacement and credited him with taking chances away, a part of his game that gets less attention. Our range: about 66 points.
headline: Ehlers is creating, and the goals should follow
